painTitle: A simple talking-head ad should not require a new editing career.
painBody: The hard part is not adding more effects. It is deciding which take is true and useful, keeping every cut natural, timing captions to the new edit, checking the output, and making revision work reusable. This packages that entire path for an agent you already use.

faqs.question: Does this replace DaVinci Resolve?
faqs.answer: No. The core path is agent-operated Kinocut, HyperFrames, and FFmpeg. The reliable handoff is a flattened master, SRT, edit plan, and receipts. Simple FCPXML is a best-effort bonus.

faqs.question: What computer does version 0.2 support?
faqs.answer: Version 0.2 supports Windows 11 x64, Apple Silicon Mac, and Intel Mac. Codex or Claude Code is also required. Linux, Windows ARM, and phone apps are not supported.

faqs.question: Is all processing offline?
faqs.answer: Transcription and rendering are local by default. Your coding agent may inspect prompts, filenames, transcripts, or project files under that provider’s terms. Optional cloud services require separate approval.

faqs.question: Will it publish my ads?
faqs.answer: No. It may prepare and render previews, but it never publishes an ad and never approves the preview for you.

faqs.question: Can it invent a stronger claim?
faqs.answer: It must not. The product preserves source meaning, checks prohibited and unsupported quantitative overlay claims, and shows uncertainty for review.

faqs.question: What is the Hook & Recording Pack?
faqs.answer: A $9 optional order bump for recording the next source clip more effectively. It is not required to make the first ad.

faqs.question: What is Ad Test Lab?
faqs.answer: A $37 optional post-purchase module for organized hook, CTA, style, and format variants after one standalone ad already works.

faqs.question: Is the person in the demo a customer?
faqs.answer: No. The presenter image and voice are synthetic demonstration media. The workflow artifacts and measured technical checks are real; no testimonial or ad-performance claim is implied.
